title: feat: shorter rules, one precedence order, no owner-typed code
headline: The rules keep what a session must do and the command to run where a script already checks the rest, say once which instructions win, and no longer assume the owner types the code; a recall run cleans up after itself and no test file can sit outside every test lane.
alignment: v1.41.0 is build 15 of the v2.0 plan: step T9, the rules diet, with the findings of the 1.40.0 install.

items.text: Rule sections a script already enforces (the merge gate, the PR body and release audits, the first push check, the commit check, sweep approval, the hand-back canary) now state the duty and the command, not what the script checks.
No rule, template or skill still asks the owner's yes before a feature-branch push or its PR; finishing a branch pushes and opens the PR by default.
One instruction order: the project's standards win for its own rules, the owner's global file for the rest, and no repo file loosens the outward-act, gate-bypass, delete or test-integrity rules.
The owner's global standards no longer assume the owner types the code: the assistant writes and runs it, one verified step at a time.
A local git act that throws away uncommitted or unpushed work is named first and waits for the owner's yes.
Three project `CLAUDE.md` hard rules that repeated `AGENTS.md` now point to it; the rules with text found nowhere else stay in full.

A dense screen splits what the user acts on now from what opens on demand, and is seen with real data early; a third manual repeat becomes a script, and a patch script that matched nothing fails [trial].
A recall run forgets its probe folder's guard record when it ends, and a cleanup that fails is named instead of hiding the run's own error.
A full or change-scoped test run refuses, and names, any test file no lane runs: one outside tests/ itself and tests/slow, one with another extension or case, or a linked folder.
From 1.41.0 every build record item says whether it reaches projects or only the kit; the 1.40.0 why-line row now says kit.
The test check keeps naming a test that fails on the old code only by a crash, held by a test of its own.
The test check measures each changed test file's flips in one CI slice, so the slow part spreads over the four slices with every check unchanged.

decisions.decision: Cut only prose a script or hook holds, and keep every duty no script checks
decisions.why: The sweep traced each cut sentence to the script line that holds it; the duties with no check stayed.

decisions.decision: The owner approved every changed rule line by pop-up
decisions.why: Text the owner approved changes only with the owner's yes; the full before and after went to the owner in one file.

decisions.decision: Flip measuring splits by test file, not by flip
decisions.why: A file's tests stay in one slice, so each verdict still sees every flip it reaches, with no job to merge slices.

verification: Each code change was seen failing on the code before it and passing after.
The rule lines were scored by the recall test against the released 1.40.0.
upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. The global `CLAUDE.md` loses its typed-code lines on `install user`; a copy you edited is merged line by line.
limits: Recall reads the project rules only, so the global `CLAUDE.md` change was checked by the owner's read, not by recall. No guard holds destructive local git yet: the rule asks for the owner's yes. The CI split gives no gain when every changed test sits in one file.
